films.title: D SPOT
films.description: Motor Lobby Skateboards' 32-minute full-length documents the growing street-skate scene in St. Petersburg, Florida. Eight credited riders carry the film, with Matt Conner leading the video and Buck Prichard and Adam Hadden contributing additional formats and footage.
creditNotes: Theories of Atlantis' authorized complete-film publication explicitly names all eight riders, credits Matt Conner with the video, Matt Conner and Buck Prichard with filming, and Adam Hadden with Super 8 footage.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies D Spot as a 32-minute full-length, corroborates the complete eight-rider roster, the production credits and St. Petersburg location.
No additional unnamed appearances are promoted into the roster; 'and more' in the publisher synopsis is not a defensible formal credit.
films.locationNote: The publisher describes D Spot as a St. Petersburg scene video, and SkateVideoSite independently maps the film to St. Petersburg.
films.historicalContext: D Spot is presented as evidence of St. Petersburg's expanding contemporary scene, giving a smaller Tampa Bay skate city a dedicated full-length rather than treating it as a stop in a broader tour video.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1920x1080 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It uses a dedicated orange-and-black d-spot title treatment over a recognizable St. Petersburg waterfront image and contains no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

films.title: POINT CLOUD
films.description: EDGLRD's 23-minute Miami full-length combines nine skaters with the visual-effects language of Harmony Korine's multimedia studio. The film preserves an unusually deep first-party production record spanning camera, edit, VFX, sound and design.
creditNotes: EDGLRD's official complete-film description supplies all nine skaters and role-specific credits for two executive producers, visuals, two principal camera operators, a team manager, ten additional filmers, editor, two producers, VFX, sound, music supervision, associate production, production coordination and product design.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies POINT CLOUD as a 23-minute full-length, corroborates the nine-rider roster, three principal filmmaker/editor credits, 28 production contributors and Miami location.
Names and spellings follow the first-party credit roll where it is more specific; no uncredited direction role is inferred.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite identifies Miami as the film's location; EDGLRD's project identity and independent filmography both frame it as the studio's Miami skate offering.
films.historicalContext: POINT CLOUD is EDGLRD's initial full-length skate-video offering, applying the studio's effects-heavy visual practice to a team film that joins local and international riders including Eric Koston, Sean Pablo and Vincent Touzery.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1920x1080 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It shows two credited skaters with POINT CLOUD's distinctive yellow sculptural mask in a fisheye street frame and contains no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

Independent filmography classifies POINT CLOUD as a 23-minute 2025 full-length, corroborates all nine skaters, 28 production contributors and Miami location, and preserves the section structure.

films.title: RUSH
films.description: Jacker's 24-minute full-length presents nine riders in a deliberately credited order of appearance. Aurélien Migaud edited and filmed the project and shares directing credit with Antony Lopez and Aurélien Courbon, supported by an extensive international camera roster.
creditNotes: Jacker's official upload and matching first-party film page provide the same nine-rider order, identify Aurélien Migaud as editor and principal filmer, name all three directors and preserve the complete additional-filming list.
Skatefolio independently corroborates Camille Bénard's additional-filming credit, and contemporary TransWorld coverage describes RUSH as Jacker's 24-minute full-length.
The first-party punctuation presents Antonio and Carreño as separate additional-filming credits; the record preserves the published credit rather than inventing a combined identity.
films.locationNote: The sources establish a multi-country European production context but do not publish a reliable complete filming itinerary, so no cities are inferred from the imagery.
films.historicalContext: RUSH established Jacker's contemporary full-length team-video identity; subsequent TransWorld coverage used it as the benchmark for the brand's position in European skateboarding and contrasted later trip edits with the completed full-length.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1920x1080 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It overlays a dedicated RUSH: A Jacker Skateboarding Film title treatment on a street-skating frame and contains no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.
